title: Improve presbyopic near vision with approved eye drops

concept.text: Provide clinically useful temporary improvement in near vision through pharmacological treatment. Pupil-modulating drops achieved this endpoint without establishing restoration of youthful accommodation. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by randomized phase 3 trials showing more participants gain at least three lines of mesopic binocular distance-corrected near visual acuity without losing more than five distance-vision letters, assessed at the prespecified post-dose time. Test set by: FDA; GEMINI efficacy assessments used day 30, hour 3. Reported achieved: FDA approved pilocarpine 1.25% (Vuity) on 29 October 2021. Sources given: [FDA Vuity clinical review](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214028Orig1s000SumR.pdf) ; [Manufacturer's dated approval announcement](https://news.abbvie.com/2021-10-29-U-S-Food-and-Drug-Administration-Approves-VUITY-TM-pilocarpine-HCI-ophthalmic-solution-1-25-%2C-the-First-and-Only-Eye-Drop-to-Treat-Presbyopia-Age-Related-Blurry-Near-Vision).

page.title: First eye drop approved to treat presbyopia
page.definition: A regulator approves an eye drop that temporarily improves near vision in adults with presbyopia, the age-related loss of the eye’s ability to focus on nearby objects. The breakthrough is the first such approval. It does not require an effect that lasts the whole day or the return of accommodation, the lens’s change of focus.

goal.need: In 2015, an estimated 826 million people worldwide had impaired near vision because they lacked adequate correction for presbyopia. Unmet need for correction was 45% (95% confidence interval, 41%–49%). Reading glasses bring small print into focus but blur more distant objects while worn. For adults who respond, a drop can make reading easier for several hours without reading glasses or surgery. Some still need glasses for part of the day.

statements.quote: Thus, there remains a need for improved methods for correcting presbyopia.

statements.quote: The overall objective of this clinical development program is to develop a fixed-dose combination of oxymetazoline and pilocarpine for the treatment of presbyopia.
statements.context: Development objective for the combination eye-drop candidate in protocol 199201-010.

completion.title: A medicines regulator grants the first marketing approval for an eye drop to treat presbyopia in adults.
completion.criterion: At least one medicines regulator grants effective marketing approval for an eye drop whose approved labeling expressly includes treatment of presbyopia in adults. The date of the first such authorization marks completion.
completion.set_by: The medicines regulator granting marketing authorization in its jurisdiction. For the US approval, the Food and Drug Administration issued the decision on NDA 214028 and approved the prescribing information.
completion.threshold_quote: It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.
completion.basis: The FDA approval letter and prescribing information establish that Vuity met the test on 28 October 2021. FDA’s review establishes priority within the United States. The two GEMINI trials supplied the efficacy evidence for that decision.

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop has nonclinical evidence sufficient for initial testing in people.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology data, together with any previous human experience, support a finding that the candidate eye drop is reasonably safe for initial testing in humans.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Investigational New Drug Application, pharmacology and toxicology studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: Nonclinical data to permit an assessment as to whether the product is reasonably safe for initial testing in humans.

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop beats vehicle on a two-line near-vision gain at most postdose measurements.
milestones.criterion: In study 199201-007, the proportion of responders at visit 3 must be statistically greater with active treatment than with vehicle. A responder gains at least two lines of dim-light, high-contrast uncorrected near visual acuity in the nondominant eye at a majority of postdose time points (at least three), relative to hour 0 of visit 1.
milestones.set_by: Allergan, study 199201-007 responder definition, reproduced in protocol 199201-009; this threshold belongs to that early study.
milestones.threshold_quote: at a majority (at least 3) of time points postdose in the nondominant eye

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop shows a near-acuity dose response at the protocol’s two-sided P ≤ 0.05 threshold.
milestones.criterion: In study 199201-009, increasing the dose must produce a statistically significant dose response in the weighted average change in uncorrected near-acuity letters read with the nondominant eye. Measurements span hours 1 through 10 over each two-day dosing period, relative to the hour 0 measurement for that period. The significance threshold is two-sided P ≤ 0.05, without adjustment for multiple tests.
milestones.set_by: Allergan, protocol 199201-009, sections 7.2 and 7.3; this statistical threshold belongs to that dose-ranging study.
milestones.threshold_quote: A 2-sided test with a p-value ≤ 0.05 will be considered statistically significant.

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop enters phase 3 testing under an effective investigational new drug application.
milestones.criterion: A participant receives the first study dose in a phase 3 presbyopia trial under an effective investigational new drug application (IND), after the required ethics approval at the site. The IND takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40, and the GEMINI phase 3 protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop beats vehicle on the three-line near-acuity response in two phase 3 studies.
milestones.criterion: In each of GEMINI 1 and GEMINI 2, the proportion of responders must be greater with the drop than with vehicle at two-sided P < 0.05. At hour 3 on day 30, a responder gains at least three lines from baseline in binocular near acuity and loses no more than one line (five letters) in binocular distance acuity. Both are measured in dim light with high-contrast charts and the same distance correction.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, statistical review of NDA 214028, documenting the composite endpoint FDA requested for GEMINI 1 and GEMINI 2.
milestones.threshold_quote: gaining 3 lines or more in mesopic, high-contrast, binocular DCNVA without losing more than 1 line (5 letters)

milestones.title: FDA accepts a new drug application for a presbyopia eye drop for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA determines that the new drug application for the presbyopia indication is sufficiently complete for substantive review, files it and notifies the applicant in writing. FDA makes the filing determination within 60 days of receiving the application.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a)(1)–(2).
milestones.threshold_quote: the NDA is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review

results.finding: In rabbits (5 per group), 1.25% AGN-190584-A was well tolerated after once-daily ocular dosing.
results.detail: The five-day study used the proposed marketed formulation. The longer pivotal ocular toxicity studies used pilocarpine with oxymetazoline.
results.quote:
Female NZW rabbits were administered vehicle or 1.25% AGN-190584-A by 
topical ocular instillation in the left eye once daily for 5 consecutive days. 
 AGN-190584-A was considered well tolerated.

results.finding: Pilocarpine plus oxymetazoline, 5–7 rabbits per sex per group, had an oxymetazoline no-observed-adverse-effect level of 0.25%.
results.detail: No histopathological changes were observed. The sponsor judged the reversible iris effects nonadverse and used the animal studies to support testing the higher pilocarpine concentration in phase 2b.
results.quote:
The no-observed-adverse-effect-level (NOAEL) was 0.25% for
oxymetazoline and 1.0% for pilocarpine (formulated with 0.5% hypromellose) when
administered twice daily.

results.finding: Pilocarpine plus oxymetazoline beat vehicle significantly on the ≥2-line near-acuity response in study 199201-007 (65 patients).
results.detail: The protocol gives neither the exact P value nor the responder percentages for the primary comparison.
results.quote:
Concurrent dosing of pilocarpine and oxymetazoline provided a statistically significant
greater response over vehicle in the percentage of patients achieving at least a 2 line
improvement in mesopic, high-contrast UNV A at a majority of time points postdose in the
nondominant eye

results.finding: Bilateral medium-dose pilocarpine/oxymetazoline (30 active, 28 vehicle) significantly beat vehicle on two-line gains through hour 8.
results.detail: Significance at each time point does not establish how many of the same participants gained two lines at a majority of time points.
results.quote: The Medium OU group was the only group to have a statistically significant percentage of participants maintain 2-line improvement at every time point on day 28 from 0.5 to 8 hours.

results.finding: Pilocarpine showed a dose response in nondominant-eye near-acuity letter gains (n = 157, P < 0.001).
results.quote:
Analysis of covariance showed that Pilo produced a significant dose response in the average increase of letters across multiple time points compared with baseline (
P
< 0.001), but Oxy concentration did not have a significant impact (
P
= 0.4797).

results.finding: In phase 3 GEMINI 1, 322 of 323 randomized participants received AGN-190584 or vehicle.
results.detail: The trial dates describe the study period. The paper gives no FDA receipt date, authorization to begin, or other documentation of IND effectiveness at first dosing.
results.quote: The safety population included 322 participants; 1 participant was excluded from the vehicle group because no treatment doses were administered.

results.finding: In GEMINI 1 (n=323), AGN-190584 beat vehicle on the day-30, hour-3 three-line near-acuity response (adjusted P<0.001).
results.detail: The three-line near-acuity endpoint was prespecified. The five-letter distance-acuity check was post hoc and left the responder counts unchanged.
results.quote: On day 30, hour 3, the percentage of participants with an improvement of 3 lines or more was 30.7% (50 of 163) in the AGN-190584 group and significantly higher compared with 8.1% (13 of 160) in the vehicle group (difference, 22.5% [95% CI, 14.3%-30.8%];  P  < .001 after multiplicity adjustment).

results.finding: Ophthalmic pilocarpine users in a 15-woman glaucoma series (4 exposed) had no observed adverse effects in themselves or their infants.
results.detail: The label also reports impaired reproductive function in rats at 18 mg/kg/day orally, about 200 times the recommended human daily dose.
results.quote:
In a retrospective case series 
of 15 women with glaucoma, 4 patients used ophthalmic pilocarpine either pre-pregnancy, during pregnancy or 
postpartum. There were no adverse effects observed in patients or in their infants.

results.finding: VUITY beat vehicle on the day-30, hour-3 responder endpoint in GEMINI 1 (n=323) and GEMINI 2 (n=427), with P < 0.01 in each.
results.detail: The FDA label expressly indicates VUITY for adult presbyopia. The October 28, 2021 timestamp dates the signature on the labeling record. The supplied text does not establish the effective approval date or that this was the first authorization.

results.finding: FDA approved Vuity eye drops for adult presbyopia effective October 28, 2021. Sample size is inapplicable to the approval decision.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon 
labeling.

results.finding: In the pilocarpine and vehicle groups (five rabbits each), ocular discomfort and hyperemia scores never exceeded +1.
results.quote: No rabbits were observed to experience any swelling or discharge, or for that matter elevated ocular discomfort or hyperemia above +1 on the respective scales.

results.finding: In Clinical Study A (17 patients), 70.6% met the visit 3 near-acuity responder endpoint with once-daily pilocarpine.
results.detail: Vehicle was administered alone in the dominant eye. The reported P-value range spans multiple visits and does not resolve the comparison at visit 3.
results.quote:
During the QD dosing period, the percentage of patients achieving the primary endpoint, at least a 2-line improvement from baseline in mesopic, high contrast UNVA (
hour
0 of visit 1) in the non-dominant eye at a majority (at least 3) of time points post dose was 70.6%.

results.finding: Clinical Study B (157 patients in the efficacy analysis) found a pilocarpine dose response in near-acuity letters (P < 0.0001).
results.quote: Overall, the response surface method analysis revealed a significant dose response driven by the pilocarpine dose (p < 0.0001 and 0.0029), which was particularly evident up to the 1% dose level.

results.finding: FDA pharmacology/toxicology reviewers found Vuity 1.25% approvable on nonclinical grounds. Nonclinical sample sizes were unstated.
results.detail: The ocular studies used pilocarpine with oxymetazoline. FDA considered the formulations sufficiently similar in excipient content to assess the ocular risk of pilocarpine monotherapy.
results.quote:
the Pharm/Tox review concluded that from the nonclinical 
pharmacology/toxicology discipline standpoint, NDA 214028 is approvable at the proposed 
dose indicated.

results.finding: In the phase 3 GEMINI presbyopia trials (749 dosed), 375 participants received pilocarpine 1.25%.
results.detail: IND 122483 is identified in the regulatory meeting history. The review gives no IND receipt date, early authorization, or site ethics approval record tied to the first dose.
results.quote:
Participants received AGN-190584 1.25% or vehicle 
dosed once daily, bilaterally, for 30 days.

results.finding: Pilocarpine 1.25% beat vehicle on the day-30, hour-3 composite response in GEMINI 1 (n=323 randomized) and GEMINI 2 (n=427 randomized), both P < 0.0001.
results.detail: The composite analysis was post hoc in GEMINI 1 and the primary analysis in GEMINI 2. One GEMINI 2 site was excluded from efficacy analyses because of incorrect acuity measurements.
results.quote:
The percent rate difference between groups (95% CI) of
15.2% (7.7, 22.7) was statistically significant (p < 0.0001) in favor of the AGN-190584 group.

results.finding: FDA found Vuity NDA 214028, received February 22, 2021, sufficient for substantive review.
results.quote: This submission was of sufficient quality to allow for a substantive review.

results.finding: Across the two phase 3 pilocarpine presbyopia trials, 749 of 750 randomized participants received at least one study dose.
Pilocarpine beat vehicle on the day-30, hour-3 response in both phase 3 trials (n=323 and n=399 analyzed, P < 0.0001 in each).
results.detail: Study 302 excluded 28 of 427 randomized participants from one site because baseline near acuity was measured with the wrong correction. Including that site as nonresponders still gave P = 0.00015.
results.quote:
The p-values from the 
Chi-squared test were < 0.0001 in both studies.

results.finding: FDA conducted substantive statistical review of VUITY NDA 214028 for adult presbyopia.
results.quote:
This document provides statistical review of the New Drug Application (NDA 214028) 
submitted by AbbVie Inc. (Applicant) to seek approval of VUITY for the treatment of near 
vision impairment associated with presbyopia in adults.

results.finding: Sequential oxymetazoline and pilocarpine eye drops in rabbits (5–7 per sex per group) yielded an oxymetazoline no-observed-adverse-effect level of 0.25%.
results.detail: The 28-day toxicity study used separate drops. The sponsor used that study, a fixed-combination pharmacokinetic comparison, and a 14-day non-GLP tolerability study to support testing a fixed formulation containing 1.5% pilocarpine in Phase 2b.
results.quote:
The no-observed-adverse-effect-level (NOAEL) was 0.25% for 
oxymetazoline and 1.0% for pilocarpine (formulated with 0.5% hypromellose) when 
administered BID.

results.finding: In study 199201-007 (n=65), pilocarpine plus oxymetazoline significantly beat vehicle on a ≥2-line near-vision gain at most postdose measurements.
results.detail: The sponsor’s protocol summary gives neither arm’s responder rate nor an exact p-value.
results.quote:
Concurrent dosing of pilocarpine and oxymetazoline provided a statistically significant 
greater response over vehicle in the percentage of patients achieving at least a 2-line 
improvement in mesopic, high contrast UNV A at a majority of timepoints postdose in the 
nondominant eye

results.finding: In the AGN-190584 presbyopia trial (163 enrolled), one repeated-measures analysis of nondominant-eye near acuity yielded P < 0.0001.
results.detail: Mean letter gains rose across AGN-190584 dose levels at every listed AGN-199201 level. The statistical-analysis listing uses the same group label for all four tests, leaving the protocol-specified dose-response P value unresolved.
results.quote: Mixed model for repeated measures · p = <0.0001 · Least squares (ls): 6.6961

results.finding: In phase 3 GEMINI 1, 22 participants with presbyopia received pilocarpine in the pharmacokinetic substudy.
results.detail: The 22 participants are the active-drug recipients sampled for pharmacokinetics. The memo gives no full trial sample size.
results.quote:
Blood 
samples for quantification of pilocarpine were collected from 22 subjects who received the 
investigational drug product.

results.finding: GEMINI 1, a phase 3 pilocarpine eye-drop trial in about 300 participants with presbyopia, began on December 21, 2018.
results.detail: The start date is reported for the study as a whole. The inspection reviewed informed consent, and a separate labeling memo cites IND 122483 in a 2021 reference. Neither establishes the required timing of site ethics approval or IND effectiveness.
results.quote:
Protocol 1883-301-013 was conducted at 36 study centers in the U.S. with approximately 300 
study subjects. The study began on 21 Dec 2018 and concluded on 31 Oct 2019.
